title: 27 common case interview mistakes (and what to do instead)
description: The mistakes almost everyone makes in case interviews, grouped by when they happen, with what to do instead.
hook: Almost everyone makes the same handful of mistakes in their first cases. That is good news, because it means they are predictable and you can avoid them. Here are the most common ones, grouped by when they happen, with what to do instead.
body:
In the first few minutes

  • Listen and take notes. Nodding along when you don’t understand, then getting lost ten minutes later. What to do instead.
  • Recap. Reading the whole prompt back word for word. What to do instead.
  • Clarifying questions (three at most). Asking a long list of questions to buy time. What to do instead.
  • Structure. Generic buckets that would fit any company, and no hypothesis. What to do instead.

In the middle of the case

  • Lead the case. Ending answers with "where would you like me to go next?" What to do instead.
  • Charts and exhibits. Describing the chart instead of drawing an insight from it. What to do instead.
  • Maths. Calculating in silence, and not checking whether the answer makes sense. What to do instead.
  • Brainstorm. Listing ideas randomly, with no priority. What to do instead.

At the end, and all the way through

  • Recommendation. Replaying the whole case from the start instead of giving the answer. What to do instead.
  • Throughout the case. Letting nerves show, and losing the link to the goal. What to do instead.

Mistakes that belong to a case type

  • Profitability. Diagnosing before splitting revenue by product / region / channel. How to avoid it.
  • Revenue drop. Explaining 'revenue' as one number. How to avoid it.
  • Market entry. Forgetting entry mode and timing; no pilot. How to avoid it.
  • Growth strategy. A list of ideas with no sizing or priority. How to avoid it.
  • M&A. Ignoring integration risk and the do-nothing option. How to avoid it.
  • Private equity. No exit thinking. How to avoid it.
  • Pricing. Using only one lens; no volume assumption. How to avoid it.
  • Competitive response. Not comparing to doing nothing. How to avoid it.
  • Investment / capacity. Approving capex before fixing bottlenecks. How to avoid it.
  • Cost & operations. Cutting costs that carry revenue. How to avoid it.
  • Market sizing. No answer hypothesis; no cross-check. How to avoid it.
  • Product launch. Choosing the 4Ps before choosing the customer. How to avoid it.
  • Valuation. Adding up future years without discounting. How to avoid it.
  • Public sector. Forcing a profit lens onto a social goal. How to avoid it.
  • Product: design. Only looking at one side of a two-sided platform. How to avoid it.
  • Product: improve / grow. Defaulting to the biggest user group. How to avoid it.
  • Product: metric drop. Guessing before segmenting. How to avoid it.

Be kind to yourself

Making these mistakes in practice is not a sign you are bad at cases. It is the point of practice. Write down the one you made after each case, and focus on just that one next time. Fixing one thing at a time is how people get good.
outro: You do not have to get all of this right at once. Pick one thing from this guide to focus on in your next practice case.
